name: Shanghai LinkWise Surxondaryo 300 MW data center
developer: Shanghai LinkWise Data Intelligence Co., Ltd.
notes: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Energy signed an MoU with Chinese firm Shanghai LinkWise Data Intelligence on 24 July 2025 for a 300 MW data center in Bukhara region, with a similar 300 MW facility planned for Surkhandarya (Surxondaryo) region (combined 600 MW program, per Ministry of Energy statements); Baxtel lists 'LinkWise: Surxondaryo' as planned for 2029. No exact site within the region or construction start announced.

name: DataVolt TAS-1 IT Park data center
developer: DataVolt (Vision Invest); DataVolt IT Park Data Center JV LLC
notes: 12 MW IT-load Tier III carrier-neutral data center at Tashkent IT Park; groundbreaking 2 May 2024, site construction from March 2025; first phase Ready-for-Service by end-2026, second phase late 2027; up to US$150M 12-year non-recourse financing from DEG, EBRD, OPEC Fund and Proparco announced 17 June 2026; ~10 MW of the 12 MW earmarked for IT equipment (StanRadar); positioned as one of Central Asia's largest AI-ready green data centers.

name: UZINFOCOM Data Center (dc.uz)
developer: Single Integrator UZINFOCOM LLC (under Ministry of Digital Technologies)
notes: UZINFOCOM operates Uzbekistan's national commercial data center at Navoi Avenue 28B, Shaykhontokhur district, Tashkent, offering colocation, cloud, hosting and monitoring; Russian trade press (IKSMEDIA) describes it as the country's first data center (initially ~20 racks, later expanded). Capacity not disclosed.

name: Uzbektelecom commercial data center (Tashkent)
notes: Russian telecom/IT trade review 'Uzbekistan: from server rooms to data centers' says the first commercial colocation data center was built by Uzbektelecom in Tashkent, following UZINFOCOM's initial facility and preceding a data center at Inha University Tashkent; capacity and exact address not disclosed.

name: East Telecom YA DC (Tashkent)
notes: Cloud provider Serverspace locates its Tashkent/Uzbekistan region in the modern 'East Telecom YA DC' data center in Tashkent; facility serves multiple hosting/cloud providers as a colocation site. Capacity and certification not disclosed.

name: Tashkent small colocation/IX facilities (Tech-TAS-233/252, ITI-IX T233/T252, Comnet Tashkent)
developer: Independent Telecom Innovations Metrotelecom; ITI-IX; IPlus
notes: DataCenterJournal directory lists five small Tashkent facilities from three providers (Tech-TAS-233, Tech-TAS-252, ITI-IX-T233, ITI-IX-T252, Comnet Tashkent); none carrier-neutral; weak directory evidence, capacity unknown; aggregate entry only.

name: Unified Data Storage and Processing Center of E-Government (Zangiata)
developer: Government of Uzbekistan (E-Government system); equipment by Huawei
notes: Official president.uz: center built in Zangiata District, Tashkent Region, launched 27 August 2022 as part of Digital Uzbekistan 2030; 20 PB capacity, 580 servers, diesel generators totalling 5 MW, certified Tier III by Uptime Institute; serves as the heart of e-government data storage/processing.

name: DataVolt New Tashkent data center campus
notes: DataVolt announced at Tashkent International Investment Forum 2025 a ~250 MW data center campus in New Tashkent (Yangi Toshkent, the new city under development in Zangiata District, Tashkent Region) within a ~500 MW Uzbekistan-wide program by 2032 (about US$3B, per NG.ru/StanRadar Aug 2026); Baxtel lists a 25-ha (62-acre) site planned for 2028. Capacity figure from forum reporting/social repost, not an official filing.
